questions.q: Comps EV/EBITDA at 8× EBITDA 42 = Rs 336 crore vs DCF 215 crore. The correct use of this gap is:
o: Trust comps — market is always right
Reconcile: growth, margin, leverage, one-offs in EBITDA (run-rate), and terminal assumptions; the bridge decides where truth sits between
questions.why: Range + drivers: normalise EBITDA (one-offs, promoter perks), cycle position of margins, D&A/capex gaps; DCF embeds specific plan growth vs comp median — never a coin-flip of the two.

questions.q: Net debt 60 crore reduces EV to equity; if the chain has Rs 25 crore unpaid promoter working-capital advances to be repaid, the equity value bridge should:
o: Treat as quasi-debt — deduct from EV to reach equity for a clean deal
questions.why: Any claim ahead of equity (quasi-debt) comes off EV; buyer's price = EV − debt − debt-like items + cash; the working-capital peg belongs in the SPA instead of the multiple.

questions.q: If a control premium of 12% is payable to the promoter seller of 60% stake, the implied price per share basis:
o: Apply to equity value at the stake level: the premium pays for control rights (board, re-strategy), not EV arithmetic
questions.why: Control premium sits at the equity/stake level (the ability to direct cash flows), while EV/DCF values the whole; minority sales would carry a discount — the mirror.

questions.q: A stock grows 8% forever with ROE 15%, and the market demands 12% return. The implied retention ratio (g = b × ROE) and the justified P/E (payout ÷ (r−g)) are:
questions.why: 8 = b × 15 ⇒ b = 53.3% ⇒ payout 46.7%; justified P/E = 0.467/(0.12−0.08) ≈ 11.8. Actual 20 ⇒ market prices expectations beyond 12% required return (or a lower r).
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the payout/retention flip inside growth equations is the trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: ROE × what you keep IS your growth; justified multiples are payout over the spread.

questions.q: RI model valuation adds book value to:
questions.why: RI: V = BV0 + Σ RI_t/(1+r)^t with RI = (ROE − r)×BV_prev; equivalence with DDM/FCFE under clean surplus.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the equivalence trio in valuation methods AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: RI says: earnings minus the charge on your capital — a profit rent, valued like any rent.

questions.q: In DCF valuation, a perpetual growth rate above the economy's long-run rate is:
o: An error — g cannot exceed nominal GDP growth perpetually
questions.why: Long-run g ≤ economy growth (else the firm would outgrow GDP forever); WACC also must exceed g for convergence.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the growth-ceiling logic check is a valuation red-flag question AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A company can outgrow the market, never the economy, forever.

questions.topic: Adjusted present vs FCFE for LBO
questions.q: Which valuation approach best fits an LBO with explicit debt schedule?
o: APV or flow-to-equity with the given debt schedule — NOT perpetuity growth
questions.why: Fixed debt schedules (LBO) favour explicit financing side effects (APV/flow-to-equity); perpetuity-growth models assume constant capital structure.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — method-to-structure matching Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Adjusted present vs FCFE for LBO
mem.tip: When debt is planned in lines, price it line by line.

questions.q: A DCF with an exit multiple for terminal value differs from perpetuity growth because:
o: It assumes a sale at a market multiple at horizon — embeds the industry P/E expectations and a finite holding period
questions.why: Terminal multiple: value = horizon-year metric × exit multiple (reflects comparable-market pricing, assumes liquidity/buyer at that date); sensitivity to both horizon length and assumed multiple.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — terminal-value-method selection with assumptions AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Gordon trusts the years after years; the multiple trusts the buyer's cheque on one year.

questions.q: A division earns NOPAT Rs 100 crore on capital employed of Rs 400 crore and reports EVA of Rs 12 crore. Its WACC must be:
questions.why: EVA = NOPAT − WACC × CE ⇒ 12 = 100 − 400w ⇒ 400w = 88 ⇒ w = 22%. The inverse-solve version tests the same single equation.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the solve-for-inverse EVA is a fresh twist AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Capital has a rent; EVA is what's left after paying it — divide the charge by the capital for the rate.
